title: Keep the access windows, the weeks off and the must-trims

blocks.text: The risk-ordered schedule went to the field, and three answers came back the same day:

**Crew supervisor:** The River circuits run through bottom land. Until the ground dries, around week 8, we can't get bucket trucks in. And K1 is at training in weeks 10 and 11; K2 is held back for storm duty in weeks 14 to 17.
**Environmental lead:** About half of the Hills circuits cross nesting habitat. No work there from week 6 to week 13.
**Compliance:** C05 and C16 are overdue on their trim cycle. They are not optional this year.

The supervisor speaks of the small season's two crews. The generator gives K1 the training weeks 10 and 11 in every season and, when a season has more than one crew, gives its last crew the storm duty in weeks 14 to 17: K2 in the small season, K6 in the medium; the tiny season's one crew has only the training weeks.

You start from the risk-ordered scheduler of the lesson before. Read three calendars, and have the generator draw them: each circuit's access windows, each crew's weeks off, and the circuits that must be trimmed this season. A trim lies wholly inside one window of its circuit, never across the closed weeks between two; a circuit whose windows are all too short for its trim waits for next season; no crew works in its weeks off; every must circuit is trimmed, and a season whose musts cannot all be trimmed is infeasible. The report marks each crew's weeks off.
**The report.** Each crew's week chart marks the crew's weeks off with `x` (a trim never covers one); the rest of every line is as before.

Run executes `main.py`, which plans the tiny season (six circuits of GridCap, a fictional utility, drawn by `vegcrew/generate.py` from seed 54) and prints the report; `expected/report.txt` is the report it should print. Submit runs every test in `tests/`, the earlier steps' included, and compares Run's report with the expected one.
Write each method below. The tests check each one by itself and the whole program end to end, so you may change any other part of the code as you see fit.

items: **Contract.** Turns a list of [first, last] pairs into a tuple of (first, last) int pairs, both weeks included.
**Modeling idea.** A calendar is data: spans of weeks, read once and kept immutable.

**Taught in** [14.1.5 Weather and Access Windows: Calendars and Optional Work](../../../../14-growing-real-projects/54-project-vegetation-crews/units/unit-05/14.1.5-weather-and-access-windows-calendars-and-optional-work.unit.html).

**Contract.** Also reads each circuit's windows (none: the whole season) and must flag (none: optional), and the season's crew_off, crew id to spans of weeks off (none: every crew works every week). Circuit gains `windows` and `must`, after `growth`; Season gains `crew_off: dict[str, Weeks]` between `months` and `circuits`, so a Season is built as Season(name, budget, crews, months, crew_off, circuits). Weeks is tuple[tuple[int, int], ...], a module-level alias in data.py.
**Modeling idea.** A missing calendar column means no calendar, so older exports still load.

**Taught in** [14.1.5 Weather and Access Windows: Calendars and Optional Work](../../../../14-growing-real-projects/54-project-vegetation-crews/units/unit-05/14.1.5-weather-and-access-windows-calendars-and-optional-work.unit.html).

items: **Contract.** Also, from its own stream named 'access', one circuit at a time in order: must when a draw of random() is below 0.15; then a River circuit has the window [8, last week], a Hills circuit has the windows [0, 5] and [14, last week] when a second draw is below 0.5, and every other circuit no windows. The season's crew_off gives K1 the weeks [10, 11] and, with more than one crew, the last crew (K2 in the small season, K6 in the medium) the weeks [14, 17]. The season's dict holds `crew_off` between `months` and `circuits`.
**Modeling idea.** A column drawn from its own stream leaves the values of every earlier column as they were.

**Taught in** [14.1.5 Weather and Access Windows: Calendars and Optional Work](../../../../14-growing-real-projects/54-project-vegetation-crews/units/unit-05/14.1.5-weather-and-access-windows-calendars-and-optional-work.unit.html).

items: **Contract.** Returns every first week that keeps a trim of the circuit's weeks inside one of its windows (the whole season when it has none) and inside the season: one interval per window long enough, and an empty domain when none is.
**Modeling idea.** An access window is a domain on the start, one interval per window, so a trim never runs across a closed week.

**Taught in** [4.5.2 Cumulative Resources: Crews and Outage Windows](../../../../04-google-or-tools-in-depth/16-cpsat-scheduling/units/unit-02/4.5.2-cumulative-resources-crews-and-outage-windows.unit.html).

**Contract.** As before, with each start taking its values from start_domain, no crew options for a circuit whose domain is empty, each crew's weeks off as fixed intervals in that crew's no-overlap, and every must circuit trimmed.
**Modeling idea.** A crew's weeks off are fixed intervals its trims may not overlap.
**Taught in** [4.5.1 Interval Variables and `NoOverlap`](../../../../04-google-or-tools-in-depth/16-cpsat-scheduling/units/unit-01/4.5.1-interval-variables-and-nooverlap.unit.html).

**Contract.** As before, keeping every calendar; when the must circuits cannot all be trimmed, a Plan with the status INFEASIBLE and no trims. (The reference also takes an `overrides` argument that it ignores, typed with a stub Override dataclass in data.py, ready for the next lesson; this step's tests do not use it.)
**Modeling idea.** A must is a hard rule, so a season that cannot keep it has no plan.

"""GridCap's vegetation crew planner.

GridCap is a fictional utility, and every season this package plans is generated from a seed by
`vegcrew.generate`. None of it is a real utility's data.
"""

"""python -m vegcrew [tiny|small|medium] [--seed N]: plan a generated season and print the plan."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse

from vegcrew.data import season_from_dict
from vegcrew.generate import SIZES, scenario
from vegcrew.planner import make_plan
from vegcrew.report import format_plan


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="vegcrew")
    parser.add_argument("size", nargs="?", default="small", choices=sorted(SIZES))
    parser.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=54)
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    season = season_from_dict(scenario(args.size, args.seed))
    print(format_plan(season, make_plan(season)))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Turn a season into a plan: each trim is one crew's run of consecutive weeks, scheduled by CP-SAT
to carry the least risk, since a circuit's risk grows every week it waits."""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field

from ortools.sat.python import cp_model

from vegcrew.data import DEFER_WEEKS, WEEKS_PER_MONTH, Circuit, Override, Season

TIME_LIMIT = 10.0                                   # seconds
WORKERS = 4                                         # parallel search workers


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Trim:
    cid: str
    crew: str                                       # K1, K2, ...
    start: int                                      # first week, counted from 0
    end: int                                        # the week after the last: end - start = weeks


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Plan:
    status: str                                     # OPTIMAL, FEASIBLE, INFEASIBLE, UNKNOWN or MODEL_INVALID
    trims: dict[str, Trim] = field(default_factory=dict)
    cost: int = 0                                   # $k spent
    risk_removed: int = 0                           # $k a year of risk the trims remove
    risk_carried: int = 0                           # $k of risk carried until each circuit is trimmed
    explanation: tuple[str, ...] = ()               # stub for lesson 14.1.6


def crew_ids(season: Season) -> list[str]:
    return [f"K{k}" for k in range(1, season.crews + 1)]


def horizon(season: Season) -> int:
    return season.months * WEEKS_PER_MONTH


@dataclass
class TrimModel:
    model: cp_model.CpModel
    trimmed: dict[str, cp_model.IntVar] = field(default_factory=dict)                 # circuit
    present: dict[tuple[str, str], cp_model.IntVar] = field(default_factory=dict)    # (circuit, crew)
    start: dict[tuple[str, str], cp_model.IntVar] = field(default_factory=dict)
    work: dict[tuple[str, str], cp_model.IntervalVar] = field(default_factory=dict)
    end: dict[str, cp_model.IntVar] = field(default_factory=dict)                     # circuit
    carried: dict[str, cp_model.IntVar] = field(default_factory=dict)                 # circuit


def start_domain(c: Circuit, h: int) -> cp_model.Domain:
    """Every first week that keeps the trim inside one of the circuit's windows and the season."""
    windows = c.windows or ((0, h - 1),)
    return cp_model.Domain.from_intervals(
        [[first, min(last, h - 1) - c.weeks + 1] for first, last in windows
         if min(last, h - 1) - c.weeks + 1 >= first])


def build(season: Season) -> TrimModel:
    tm = TrimModel(cp_model.CpModel())
    h = horizon(season)
    deferred = h + DEFER_WEEKS                      # the end week of a circuit left for next season
    for c in season.circuits:
        t = tm.trimmed[c.cid] = tm.model.new_bool_var(f"t_{c.cid}")
        e = tm.end[c.cid] = tm.model.new_int_var_from_domain(
            cp_model.Domain.from_intervals([[c.weeks, h], [deferred, deferred]]), f"e_{c.cid}")
        starts = start_domain(c, h)
        options = [] if starts.is_empty() else crew_ids(season)    # no window fits it: no options
        for k in options:
            p = tm.present[c.cid, k] = tm.model.new_bool_var(f"p_{c.cid}_{k}")
            s = tm.start[c.cid, k] = tm.model.new_int_var_from_domain(starts, f"s_{c.cid}_{k}")   # window_c
            tm.work[c.cid, k] = tm.model.new_optional_fixed_size_interval_var(s, c.weeks, p, f"w_{c.cid}_{k}")
            tm.model.add(e == s + c.weeks).only_enforce_if(p)                        # ends_c,k
        tm.model.add(sum(tm.present[c.cid, k] for k in options) == t)               # once_c
        tm.model.add(e == deferred).only_enforce_if(~t)                              # waits_c
        if c.must:
            tm.model.add(t == 1)                                                     # must_c
        table = [c.carried(week) for week in range(deferred + 1)]
        tm.carried[c.cid] = tm.model.new_int_var(0, table[-1], f"r_{c.cid}")
        tm.model.add_element(e, table, tm.carried[c.cid])                            # risk_c
    for k in crew_ids(season):
        off = [tm.model.new_fixed_size_interval_var(first, last - first + 1, f"off_{k}_{first}")
               for first, last in season.crew_off.get(k, ())]
        tm.model.add_no_overlap([w for (_, crew), w in tm.work.items() if crew == k] + off)   # crew_k
    tm.model.add(sum(c.cost * tm.trimmed[c.cid] for c in season.circuits) <= season.budget)   # budget
    tm.model.minimize(sum(tm.carried.values()))
    return tm


def check_overrides(season: Season, overrides: tuple[Override, ...]) -> list[str]:
    """Stub for lesson 14.1.6."""
    return []


def make_plan(season: Season, overrides: tuple[Override, ...] = ()) -> Plan:
    """Choose the circuits to trim, the crew for each and its weeks: the least risk carried through the
    season and the wait for the next, within the budget, one crew per trim, one trim per crew at a time,
    every trim inside one of its circuit's windows and outside its crew's weeks off, every must trimmed."""
    tm = build(season)
    solver = cp_model.CpSolver()
    solver.parameters.max_time_in_seconds = TIME_LIMIT
    solver.parameters.num_workers = WORKERS
    status = solver.status_name(solver.solve(tm.model))
    if status not in ("OPTIMAL", "FEASIBLE"):
        return Plan(status)
    trims = {}
    for (cid, k), p in tm.present.items():
        if solver.boolean_value(p):
            start = solver.value(tm.start[cid, k])
            trims[cid] = Trim(cid, k, start, start + season.circuit(cid).weeks)
    chosen = [season.circuit(cid) for cid in trims]
    return Plan(status, trims, cost=sum(c.cost for c in chosen), risk_removed=sum(c.risk for c in chosen),
                risk_carried=round(solver.objective_value))

"""The plan as the vegetation manager reads it: one line per crew, one letter per week."""

from __future__ import annotations

from vegcrew.data import Season
from vegcrew.planner import Plan, crew_ids, horizon


def format_plan(season: Season, plan: Plan) -> str:
    lines = [f"season {season.name}: {len(season.circuits)} circuits, budget ${season.budget:,}k, "
             f"crews {season.crews}, weeks {horizon(season)}",
             f"status {plan.status}: {len(plan.trims)} trims, cost ${plan.cost:,}k, "
             f"risk carried ${plan.risk_carried:,}k"]
    for k in crew_ids(season):
        trims = sorted((t for t in plan.trims.values() if t.crew == k), key=lambda t: t.start)
        week = ["."] * horizon(season)
        for first, last in season.crew_off.get(k, ()):
            week[first:last + 1] = "x" * (last - first + 1)
        for t in trims:
            week[t.start:t.end] = t.cid[-1] * (t.end - t.start)
        lines.append(f"  {k} {''.join(week)}  " + " ".join(f"{t.cid}:{t.start}-{t.end - 1}" for t in trims))
    return "\n".join(lines)

"""Turn a season into a plan: each trim is one crew's run of consecutive weeks, scheduled by CP-SAT
to carry the least risk, since a circuit's risk grows every week it waits."""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field

from ortools.sat.python import cp_model

from vegcrew.data import DEFER_WEEKS, WEEKS_PER_MONTH, Season

TIME_LIMIT = 10.0                                   # seconds
WORKERS = 4                                         # parallel search workers


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Trim:
    cid: str
    crew: str                                       # K1, K2, ...
    start: int                                      # first week, counted from 0
    end: int                                        # the week after the last: end - start = weeks


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Plan:
    status: str                                     # OPTIMAL, FEASIBLE, INFEASIBLE, UNKNOWN or MODEL_INVALID
    trims: dict[str, Trim] = field(default_factory=dict)
    cost: int = 0                                   # $k spent
    risk_removed: int = 0                           # $k a year of risk the trims remove
    risk_carried: int = 0                           # $k of risk carried until each circuit is trimmed


def crew_ids(season: Season) -> list[str]:
    return [f"K{k}" for k in range(1, season.crews + 1)]


def horizon(season: Season) -> int:
    return season.months * WEEKS_PER_MONTH


@dataclass
class TrimModel:
    model: cp_model.CpModel
    trimmed: dict[str, cp_model.IntVar] = field(default_factory=dict)                 # circuit
    present: dict[tuple[str, str], cp_model.IntVar] = field(default_factory=dict)    # (circuit, crew)
    start: dict[tuple[str, str], cp_model.IntVar] = field(default_factory=dict)
    work: dict[tuple[str, str], cp_model.IntervalVar] = field(default_factory=dict)
    end: dict[str, cp_model.IntVar] = field(default_factory=dict)                     # circuit
    carried: dict[str, cp_model.IntVar] = field(default_factory=dict)                 # circuit


def build(season: Season) -> TrimModel:
    tm = TrimModel(cp_model.CpModel())
    h = horizon(season)
    deferred = h + DEFER_WEEKS                      # the end week of a circuit left for next season
    for c in season.circuits:
        t = tm.trimmed[c.cid] = tm.model.new_bool_var(f"t_{c.cid}")
        e = tm.end[c.cid] = tm.model.new_int_var_from_domain(
            cp_model.Domain.from_intervals([[c.weeks, h], [deferred, deferred]]), f"e_{c.cid}")
        options = crew_ids(season) if c.weeks <= h else []          # too long for the season: no options
        for k in options:
            p = tm.present[c.cid, k] = tm.model.new_bool_var(f"p_{c.cid}_{k}")
            s = tm.start[c.cid, k] = tm.model.new_int_var(0, h - c.weeks, f"s_{c.cid}_{k}")
            tm.work[c.cid, k] = tm.model.new_optional_fixed_size_interval_var(s, c.weeks, p, f"w_{c.cid}_{k}")
            tm.model.add(e == s + c.weeks).only_enforce_if(p)                        # ends_c,k
        tm.model.add(sum(tm.present[c.cid, k] for k in options) == t)               # once_c
        tm.model.add(e == deferred).only_enforce_if(~t)                              # waits_c
        table = [c.carried(week) for week in range(deferred + 1)]
        tm.carried[c.cid] = tm.model.new_int_var(0, table[-1], f"r_{c.cid}")
        tm.model.add_element(e, table, tm.carried[c.cid])                            # risk_c
    for k in crew_ids(season):
        tm.model.add_no_overlap(w for (_, crew), w in tm.work.items() if crew == k)     # crew_k
    tm.model.add(sum(c.cost * tm.trimmed[c.cid] for c in season.circuits) <= season.budget)   # budget
    tm.model.minimize(sum(tm.carried.values()))
    return tm


def make_plan(season: Season) -> Plan:
    """Choose the circuits to trim, the crew for each and its weeks: the least risk carried through the
    season and the wait for the next, within the budget, one crew per trim, one trim per crew at a time."""
    tm = build(season)
    solver = cp_model.CpSolver()
    solver.parameters.max_time_in_seconds = TIME_LIMIT
    solver.parameters.num_workers = WORKERS
    status = solver.status_name(solver.solve(tm.model))
    if status not in ("OPTIMAL", "FEASIBLE"):
        return Plan(status)
    trims = {}
    for (cid, k), p in tm.present.items():
        if solver.boolean_value(p):
            start = solver.value(tm.start[cid, k])
            trims[cid] = Trim(cid, k, start, start + season.circuit(cid).weeks)
    chosen = [season.circuit(cid) for cid in trims]
    return Plan(status, trims, cost=sum(c.cost for c in chosen), risk_removed=sum(c.risk for c in chosen),
                risk_carried=round(solver.objective_value))


def start_domain(c: Circuit, h: int) -> cp_model.Domain:
    """Returns every first week that keeps a trim of the circuit's weeks inside one of its windows (the whole season when it has none) and inside the season: one interval per window long enough, and an empty domain when none is."""
    return cp_model.Domain.from_intervals([])

"""The plan as the vegetation manager reads it: one line per crew, one letter per week."""

from __future__ import annotations

from vegcrew.data import Season
from vegcrew.planner import Plan, crew_ids, horizon


def format_plan(season: Season, plan: Plan) -> str:
    lines = [f"season {season.name}: {len(season.circuits)} circuits, budget ${season.budget:,}k, "
             f"crews {season.crews}, weeks {horizon(season)}",
             f"status {plan.status}: {len(plan.trims)} trims, cost ${plan.cost:,}k, "
             f"risk carried ${plan.risk_carried:,}k"]
    for k in crew_ids(season):
        trims = sorted((t for t in plan.trims.values() if t.crew == k), key=lambda t: t.start)
        week = ["."] * horizon(season)
        for t in trims:
            week[t.start:t.end] = t.cid[-1] * (t.end - t.start)
        lines.append(f"  {k} {''.join(week)}  " + " ".join(f"{t.cid}:{t.start}-{t.end - 1}" for t in trims))
    return "\n".join(lines)
